questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Using my studies to explore new parts of the world. I had been in Mexico for a few weeks previously years back, and this was an opportunity to go back and get a deeper understanding and connection to the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing experience. Before I left for Mexico I thought I would want to use my exchange as an opportunity to travel around and explore Mexico (which I also did), but the most fulfilling thing for me was the close friendships I developed and having the opportunity to live my everyday life in Cholula and become part of the local area. It's a really good opportunity to meet a lot of people from different countries and there are a lot social events for exchange students etc that make this even more uncomplicated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There are some pre-departure meetings where you get a lot of information from counselors and tutors. During these meetings you also become a part of a Whatsapp group for exchange students which is also good for information, available housing, events etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As previously mentioned

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy! I found mine through the Whatsapp group where they posted some of the available housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about finding housing before coming. There are a lot of options depending on what you want to get out of your stay and they can also be very cheap. I lived in a house with three other exchange students where we all had our own rooms, shared kitchen and living room for around 1500 kr pr month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are different housing organizations that are competing with each other. My housing was through Cholula Capital. The landlord Ray is in my opinion a little shady/manipulative but the stay was really nice as we had a really good vibe in our house. If it is still possible to rent a room in Casa Ocho it is definitely recommendable.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If i remember correctly I think it was an okay easy process. You also talk to other exchange students who are in the same situation as you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have counselors you can talk to about courses on email or in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not many of the courses were related to my studies, so I tried some that were more or less random. After sitting in the different classes, I ended up changing some of the courses to ones that I found more interesting and that fit with the schedule I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the process and the information you get and talk to the other exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience at UDLAP was okay. The classes and style of teaching are very similar to gymnasiet, and they take attendance which can be a little rough when being used to the more "free" style of studying in Denmark. But you get used to it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As the courses I took were not really in the area of my studies, it is hard to compare levels, but I didn't put much work in academically during this semester and ended up passing all my courses with no problems. The teachers are likely also more chill because you are an exchange student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Communication and globalization, Project management in creative teams, Market intelligence, Socio-educational theories, EU studies

Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.answer: Check out other parts of Mexico, party, and drink some pulque.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. People are nice and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: No matter how you choose to spend your exchange you will get something out of it. There are a lot of opportunities to make friends, personal development, party, learn Spanish, travel Mexico, experience cultural events etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open, and be open toward the possibility that your initial thoughts/plans of how you wanted your exchange semester to go can change. I didn't know what I wanted out of my exchange semester until after being more settled here. Enjoy it, it really is an amazing experience on so many levels.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The close friendships i developed.
